reason: Dumuzid is the Sumerian shepherd-god of vegetation and the sheepfold; milk, wool, date palms, and seasonal fertility are his canonical domain, making agriculture the primary industry fit.
The pastoral economy supplies milk, cheese, and meat; Dumuzid's sacred-marriage feast turns the products of the flock into the institutional table.
Mesopotamian wedding and New Year liturgy involved beer and date-palm wine; Dumuzid's bridal songs belong to the feast and hospitality tradition.
His half-year sojourn in the underworld and the ancient laments for Tammuz map directly onto mourning, memorial rites, and the seasonal remembrance of loss.
